narratives.Overview:
## Summary

CodeQL open alert on default branch: **HIGH** `js/polynomial-redos` — Polynomial regular expression used on uncontrolled data.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Alert | [#112](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/112) |
| Rule | `js/polynomial-redos` |
| Severity | HIGH |
| Location | `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/greptile-detector.ts` ~L301 |
| Message | This regular expression that depends on library input may run slow on strings starting with 'Last reviewed commit:[' and with many repetitions of 'Last reviewed commit:['. |

## What to build

Rewrite or bound the flagged site so CodeQL `js/polynomial-redos` clears for this alert (or document accepted risk with suppress + rationale if false positive after review). Prefer a real fix over suite-config changes.

## Acceptance

- [ ] CodeQL alert [#112](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/112) clears on master (auto-close or dismiss with reason after fix).
- [ ] Existing unit tests for the touched module still pass; add adversarial input coverage if useful.
- [ ] CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed entry citing CodeQL alert #112.

## Non-goals

- Changing CodeQL suite config as the primary fix.
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue (siblings tracked separately).

## In plain English
CodeQL alert #112 flags MARKDOWN_LINK_SHA_RE in greptile-detector.ts: the unbounded `\[.*?\]` after `Last reviewed commit:` can run slow on adversarial review bodies that repeat `Last reviewed commit:[`. Prefer-A clears that by rewriting or bounding the parse so polynomial ReDoS is gone, keeps existing Last-reviewed SHA fixtures green, and rejects CodeQL suite-config or suppress-only as the primary fix.

## Draft remedy sketch
1. Rewrite or bound MARKDOWN_LINK_SHA_RE so link-text matching cannot backtrack unboundedly (bounded character class for link text, possessive/atomic equivalent, or a two-step locate-then-bounded-link parse). Keep parseLastReviewedShaMarkdownLink / parseLastReviewedShaNaiveInline behavior for current fixtures (escaped brackets, AC4 markdown-link and inline forms).
2. Add adversarial coverage that would hang or thrash under the old `.*?` form if useful; existing greptile-detector unit tests must still pass.
3. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed citing CodeQL alert #112 and #5742.
4. Keep-outs: CodeQL suite-config / path keep-out as primary clearance; suppress-only without rewrite/bound; bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts; changing Greptile/SLizard detection semantics beyond the Last-reviewed SHA parse site.

## Reject (draft)
- CodeQL suite-config or path keep-out as the primary fix
- Suppress-only / accepted-risk dismiss without a rewrite or bound at the flagged site
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts into this issue
- Changing Greptile detector tier/badge/confidence semantics beyond Last-reviewed SHA parse
- Leaving unbounded `.*?` in place because review bodies are 'usually trusted'

Round 1 fresh critic; open critique; arc-mode: no-ingest. Reviewed Prefer-A [6256512699](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/5742#issuecomment-6256512699), Stop 1 [6256515021](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/5742#issuecomment-6256515021), and panel-deposit 6256517263 within envelope ceiling 6256517263.

Verdict: no blocks-the-design finding. Rewrite/bound is viable; the draft is not evidence that a particular replacement clears the alert. Three sharpens-framing findings follow.

Verification and inventory: pin-read with git show at 8341f369ccc55fa907abd5e575bb29556e467e9f. The [detector](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/8341f369ccc55fa907abd5e575bb29556e467e9f/packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/greptile-detector.ts#L58-L60) has separate MARKDOWN_LINK_SHA_RE and NAIVE_INLINE_SHA_RE; their exported parsers return the capture or null. simulatePollLoop uses the markdown parser for body SHA, with existing SHA-currency and clean-gate machinery downstream. Escaped-bracket and AC4 fixtures already cover the important behavior; extend those tests rather than introduce another parser interface or polling policy. REST GET of [alert #112](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/code-scanning/112) confirms open js/polynomial-redos on this exact commit, exec site line 301, regex span line 60, and the repeated Last-reviewed-prefix witness. The alert site really is the unbounded lazy link-text form.

1. **sharpens-framing — State a whole-search work bound.** Evidence: the unanchored regex retries successive Last-reviewed markers, each of which can inspect the remaining suffix. Repeated `Last reviewed commit:[` with no closing link creates overlapping scans. A two-step implementation that locates every marker and searches each remaining suffix for a delimiter can retain quadratic work without a regex. Consequence: keep Prefer-A, but require a fixed candidate window with explicit over-limit behavior, or a monotonic scan with linear total work; specify advancement after malformed candidates. Cover repeated markers with no terminator and malformed candidates followed by a valid link. A fixed bound is the smallest credible alternative to a scanner when the length limit and boundary behavior are accepted. A scanner becomes preferable if arbitrary-length compatible labels must remain supported.

2. **sharpens-framing — Preserve deliberate non-matches as well as successful extraction.** Evidence: [swarm_poller_template.test.ts lines 300–356](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/8341f369ccc55fa907abd5e575bb29556e467e9f/packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/swarm_poller_template.test.ts#L300-L356) demonstrates that a simple negated-closing-bracket matcher rejects BODY_ESCAPED_BRACKET_LINK_TEXT. Bounding that character class does not restore escaped-bracket support. Tests require markdown-link and escaped-label bodies to exit CLEAN in one poll. AC4 inline-only returns a SHA from the naive parser but null from the markdown parser, then STALL after three polls with sha_match. Third-confidence-form remains STALL with confidence; empty/truncated remain non-clean. Failure mode: interpreting “inline forms preserved” as permission for inline fallback changes SHA authority. Consequence: retain the separate parser contracts and these outcomes; accommodate the escaped-bracket fixture. Renaming a “non_greedy” test may be appropriate, but weakening its behavior assertion is not.

3. **sharpens-framing — Separate feasibility from clearance evidence.** Evidence: the draft offers alternatives, not an executable replacement; alert #112 remains open at the dispatch SHA. Fixture success alone establishes neither complexity nor CodeQL clearance. Failure mode: accepting removal of `.*?` or a fast small example as remediation proof. Consequence: retain the issue's explicit CodeQL acceptance condition under the existing analysis configuration, and require adversarial regression coverage for the chosen algorithm alongside existing tests and the CHANGELOG entry. No suite-config or suppress-only primary fix is needed. This critique inspected pinned source and test assertions; it did not execute the suite or replacement CodeQL analysis and claims neither has passed.

Untrusted-input lens: review-body text is uncontrolled library input even when presented as a Greptile summary. It must not cause unbounded parsing work or broaden which SHA evidence satisfies the clean gate. No new concurrency mechanism calls for a separate swarm design.

Process-only critique complete. No product implementation or ingestion performed.

## In plain English
Clear CodeQL alert #112 by rewriting the Last-reviewed markdown-link SHA parse so whole-search work is bounded (no unbounded `.*?` / unbounded two-step suffix scans), keep the separate markdown vs naive parser contracts and today's deliberate non-matches (including escaped-bracket CLEAN and AC4 inline STALL), prove the chosen algorithm with adversarial regression plus existing tests, and land a CHANGELOG Security/Fixed entry. Suite-config or suppress-only stays rejected as primary.

## Bound remedy

relieves: P1
- Bound whole-search Last-reviewed markdown-link SHA parse: replace MARKDOWN_LINK_SHA_RE unbounded `\[.*?\]` with a fixed candidate window (explicit over-limit → null) or a monotonic linear scan that advances after malformed candidates; total work must be linear in body length. Cover repeated `Last reviewed commit:[` with no terminator and a malformed candidate followed by a valid link. Keep NAIVE_INLINE_SHA_RE as the separate inline path.
- Preserve deliberate non-matches and SHA authority: retain separate parseLastReviewedShaMarkdownLink vs parseLastReviewedShaNaiveInline contracts; escaped-bracket markdown-link bodies must still extract SHA / CLEAN as today; AC4 inline-only must stay null on the markdown parser (naive may return SHA) without inventing markdown→inline fallback that widens SHA authority; AC4 third-confidence / empty / truncated outcomes unchanged. Extend existing fixtures rather than a new parser interface or polling policy.
- Clearance evidence: adversarial regression for the chosen algorithm (repeated markers / no terminator / malformed-then-valid) alongside existing greptile-detector / swarm_poller_template tests; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Security/Fixed citing CodeQL alert #112 and #5742; alert #112 must clear under the existing analysis configuration after the rewrite (fixture speed alone is not clearance proof).

## Reject
- CodeQL suite-config or path keep-out as the primary fix
- Suppress-only / accepted-risk dismiss without rewrite/bound at the flagged site
- Two-step locate-every-marker + unbounded suffix search that retains quadratic work
- Collapsing markdown-link and naive-inline into one parser or adding inline fallback that widens SHA authority
- Weakening escaped-bracket / AC4 non-match assertions
- Bundling unrelated code-scanning alerts
- Changing Greptile tier/badge/confidence / clean-gate semantics beyond Last-reviewed SHA parse
- Treating removal of `.*?` or a fast small example as CodeQL clearance proof without alert #112 clearing under existing config

## Takes
- Codex F1 whole-search bound: accept-into-contract — remint Bound limb requiring fixed window or linear monotonic scan + repeated-marker / malformed-then-valid coverage
- Codex F2 deliberate non-matches / SHA authority: accept-into-contract — remint Bound limb preserving separate parsers, escaped-bracket CLEAN, AC4 inline STALL without markdown→inline fallback
- Codex F3 feasibility vs clearance: accept-into-contract — remint Bound limb requiring adversarial regression + CHANGELOG + alert clear under existing analysis config

Forward verdict: accept-into-contract. Next under yolo: pain-audit of Prefer-A Bound against pain-P1.

The pinned [regex and separate inline matcher](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/8341f369ccc55fa907abd5e575bb29556e467e9f/packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/greptile-detector.ts#L58-L60) substantiate the pain: repeated Last-reviewed prefixes can cause successive failed candidates to rescan overlapping suffixes through the unbounded lazy label match. A fixed candidate window with explicit over-limit rejection or a monotonic linear scan, together with the explicit linear-total-work requirement, excludes the unbounded two-step suffix-search substitute. Repeated-marker/no-terminator and malformed-then-valid coverage target both the complexity failure and recovery behavior.

Bound limb 2 preserves the existing authority boundary on uncontrolled review-body text. The separate exported parsers remain separate; the pinned escaped-bracket fixture must still extract its SHA and CLEAN, while AC4 inline-only stays null in the markdown parser and STALL at the clean gate. Bound limb 3 makes actual alert #112 clearance under the existing analysis configuration an implementation obligation, alongside adversarial regressions and the existing suites. This closes Round-1's feasibility-versus-clearance gap without treating a small fast example, quantifier removal, suppression, or suite exclusion as proof.

This is clearance of the proposed remedy's coverage of P1, not a claim that the vulnerability is already fixed or CodeQL has passed. No replacement was implemented, and no tests or replacement CodeQL analysis were executed. Process-only audit complete; no ingest or repository changes.
